units.text: Refute-first sweep of landed work, one phase - Read, Break or Drive - on one area.
Use when an inquisition's captain sends you a phase and an area.

rules.rule: The inquisitor skill is used when an inquisition captain sends a phase (Read, Break or Drive) and an area.

units.text: Catch what got through - and refute every catch before it counts.

The brief: your phase, your area with its map row and register entries, the audit SHA and landing base, the governing intent, your worktree, your context limit, and for Break the proof branch, for Drive the verification skill and the API base.

rules.rule: The captain sends each inquisitor a brief naming its phase, area with map row and register entries, audit SHA and landing base, governing intent, worktree, context limit, and for Break the proof branch, for Drive the verification skill and the API base.

units.text: Your phase's checklist: [read](resources/read.md), [break](resources/break.md) or [drive](resources/drive.md).

rules.rule: An inquisitor reads the checklist of its own phase: read, break or drive.

units.text: [context-size](resources/context-size.md), the command you run after each work item.

rules.rule: An inquisitor runs the context-size command after each work item.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/understand/about.md`.

rules.rule: An inquisitor reads dydo/understand/about.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/understand/architecture.md`.

rules.rule: An inquisitor reads dydo/understand/architecture.md from the repository root.

units.text: From the repository root, read `dydo/guides/coding-standards.md`.

rules.rule: An inquisitor reads dydo/guides/coding-standards.md from the repository root.

units.text: You are a worker: one phase, one area, one return to the captain who sent you.

rules.rule: An inquisitor is a worker: one phase, one area, one return to the captain who sent it.

units.text: Read and Drive change nothing in the repository.

rules.rule: Read and Drive change nothing in the repository.

units.text: Break writes tests on its proof branch, and touches test paths only.

rules.rule: Break writes tests on its proof branch and touches test paths only.

units.text: The captain files tickets, prepares patches and keeps the register; your output is the return.

rules.rule: The captain files tickets, prepares patches and keeps the register; the inquisitor outputs only its return.

units.text: A question goes back to the captain with what you searched.

rules.rule: A question goes back to the captain with what the inquisitor searched.

units.text: **Work the area's items in order.**

rules.rule: Work the area items in order.

units.text: Run your phase's checklist: discovery, then work, then document.

rules.rule: Run the phase checklist in order: discovery, then work, then document.

units.text: Your work items are what discovery lists: Read's files, Break's hypotheses, Drive's journeys, each with the routed register entries.

notRule.note: work items are what discovery lists

units.text: A follow-up or hand-back brief names your items; work only those.

rules.rule: On a follow-up or hand-back brief, work only the items it names.

units.text: Done when each item's entries for your return are written.

rules.rule: A work item is done when its entries for the return are written.

units.text: **Read your context size** after each work item with [context-size](resources/context-size.md).

rules.rule: After each work item read the context size with the context-size resource.

units.text: Past your limit, stop: the item you just documented is your last.

rules.rule: Past the context limit, stop: the item just documented is the last.

units.text: Done when you have either started the next item under the limit or stopped over it.
**Return.**
Done when every work item is documented or listed as handed back.

rules.rule: The return step is done when every work item is documented or listed as handed back.

units.text: Run every probe, test and drive capped: `[env MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0 UseSharedCompilation=false] systemd-run --user --scope --slice=<agent slice> -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue timeout 3600 <cmd>`, a probe at 4G with a short timeout.

rules.rule: Run every probe, test and drive capped: [env MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0 UseSharedCompilation=false] systemd-run --user --scope --slice=<agent slice> -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue timeout 3600 <cmd>, a probe at 4G with a short timeout.

units.text: A cap hit is a finding; never raise the cap.

rules.rule: A cap hit is a finding; never raise the cap.

units.text: Use your session's agent slice: the nearest `.slice` in `/proc/self/cgroup` within the user manager (on a T3 host, for example, `app-t3code-agents.slice`; a nearer session slice takes precedence).

rules.rule: Use the session agent slice: the nearest .slice in /proc/self/cgroup within the user manager (on a T3 host, e.g. app-t3code-agents.slice; a nearer session slice takes precedence).

units.text: Omit `--slice` where no agent slice exists.

rules.rule: Omit --slice where no agent slice exists.

units.text: Use the bracketed env prefix for .NET commands, without the brackets.

rules.rule: Use the bracketed env prefix for .NET commands, without the brackets.

units.text: A finding counts once the repository proves it on the audit SHA:

rules.rule: A finding counts once the repository proves it on the audit SHA, by the proof its type requires.

units.text: | Behaviour in code | a red test committed on the proof branch: its SHA and test name | Break |

rules.rule: Behaviour in code is proved by a red test committed on the proof branch: its SHA and test name (Break).

units.text: | Behaviour through the app | rerunnable drive steps with the observed and the expected output | Drive |

rules.rule: Behaviour through the app is proved by rerunnable drive steps with observed and expected output (Drive).

units.text: | Missed intent, a DR or standard broken, a wrong comment, a prose contradiction | both passages quoted at `file:line` | Read |

rules.rule: Missed intent, a broken DR or standard, a wrong comment or a prose contradiction is proved by both passages quoted at file:line (Read).

units.text: | Unused member, export or field | its definition at `file:line` and a reference search, command and output quoted, finding no caller outside the tests; a test is not a caller | Read |

rules.rule: An unused member, export or field is proved by its definition at file:line and a quoted reference search (command and output) finding no caller outside tests; a test is not a caller (Read).

units.text: | Nit | none; a nit needs no proof | any |

rules.rule: A nit needs no proof.

units.text: A finding you see but cannot prove in your phase gets a tag: `testable` for Break, `drivable` for Drive.

rules.rule: A finding seen but not provable in the phase gets a tag: testable for Break, drivable for Drive.

units.text: Tag it and move on.
The three review severities, judged against the source, not against how sure you feel:

rules.rule: Judge the three severities against the source, not against how sure you feel.

units.text: **blocker** - the intended case is wrong: data loss, corruption, a security hole, a broken journey.

rules.rule: Blocker: the intended case is wrong (data loss, corruption, security hole, broken journey).

units.text: **should** - a real bug callers will hit inside the intent.

rules.rule: Should: a real bug callers will hit inside the intent.

units.text: A verification gap is a should.

rules.rule: A verification gap is a should.

units.text: **nit** - everything else: another code path, a rare case, a small cost, style.

rules.rule: Nit: everything else (another code path, rare case, small cost, style).

units.text: **Reachable and concrete.**

rules.rule: A finding must be reachable and concrete: "under X this returns or corrupts Y", a sequence someone hits.

units.text: "Under X this returns or corrupts Y": a sequence someone hits.
**New or pre-existing.**

rules.rule: Say whether a finding is new or pre-existing; work that merely exposed an older defect is worth reporting.

units.text: Work that merely exposed an older defect is worth reporting; say which.
**One bug, one finding.**

rules.rule: One bug, one finding: a bug already in the area register entries is a sighting, added with where seen and proof under its register ID.

units.text: A bug already in your area's register entries is a sighting: add where you saw it and your proof, under its register ID.
**A clean area reports nothing.**

rules.rule: A clean area reports nothing.

units.text: A return with only real problems, or none, has succeeded.
To the captain, in this shape; an empty list is written `none`:

rules.rule: The inquisitor returns to the captain in the given shape; an empty list is written none.

units.text:
```text
Phase <read|break|drive>; area <ID>; handed back <items or none>; context <tokens> of <limit>; inquisitor/model: <identity>.
Findings:
1. <title>; severity <blocker|should|nit>; where `file:line`; wrong: <the wrong outcome in one sentence>; proof: <per the Proof table, or tagged testable|drivable>.
Sightings:
1. <register ID>; where `file:line`; proof: <per the Proof table>.
Not reproduced:
1. <register ID or your hypothesis>; observed: <the deciding observation>.
Unreachable:
1. <journey>; prerequisite: <what it needs>; route tried: <what you tried>.
```
The second phase, wherever the landing changed behaviour.
Break forms hypotheses about how the area fails and decides each with a test it writes itself, on its proof branch.

rules.rule: Break forms hypotheses about how the area fails and decides each with a test it writes itself on its proof branch.

units.text: Prove three things and return a failure to the captain instead of working around it:

rules.rule: Return a failed worktree check to the captain instead of working around it.

units.text: `HEAD` is on the proof branch your brief names, `proof/<KEY>-<area>-<n>`, cut from the audit SHA.

rules.rule: HEAD is on the proof branch the brief names, proof/<KEY>-<area>-<n>, cut from the audit SHA.

units.text: The worktree is clean.

rules.rule: Before editing, Break proves the worktree is clean.

units.text: Every path you will touch is a test path: a test project, a test folder or a test file.

rules.rule: Every path touched is a test path: a test project, folder or file.

units.text: **Read the area for how it fails.**

rules.rule: Read the area for how it fails: inputs, states, error paths, boundaries, concurrency and seams it calls through.

units.text: Its inputs, states, error paths, boundaries, concurrency and the seams it calls through.
Done when you can name where the area's behaviour can go wrong.
**List the hypotheses.**

rules.rule: List the hypotheses: the inquisitor's own plus every register entry for the area tagged testable.

units.text: Yours, plus every register entry for the area tagged `testable`.
Each names the suspected failure, the seam, the input or state, the expected observation, and the test that would refute it.

rules.rule: Each hypothesis names the suspected failure, the seam, the input or state, the expected observation and the test that would refute it.

units.text: Done when every tagged entry and every hypothesis of yours is on the list.
**Write one test per hypothesis** in the project's own test framework, at a test path, through the area's public seam where one exists, and run only that test.

rules.rule: Write one test per hypothesis in the project's own test framework, at a test path, through the area's public seam where one exists, and run only that test.

units.text: Done when each test has run.
**Read the verdict.**
**Red, failing for the stated reason:** confirmed.

rules.rule: A test that is red and fails for the stated reason means confirmed.

units.text: Commit the test alone as `<KEY> proof: <hypothesis>` and note the SHA.

rules.rule: Commit a confirmed test alone as "<KEY> proof: <hypothesis>" and note the SHA.

units.text: **Green:** not reproduced.

rules.rule: A green test means not reproduced.

units.text: Discard the test; note the observation.

rules.rule: For a not-reproduced hypothesis discard the test and note the observation.

units.text: **Red for another reason, or undecidable:** inconclusive.

rules.rule: A test red for another reason or undecidable means inconclusive.

units.text: Discard the test; note the deciding observation.

rules.rule: For an inconclusive hypothesis discard the test and note the deciding observation.

units.text: A test that needs a sleep or a timeout is wrong; force races with fake timers or interleaving.

rules.rule: A test that needs a sleep or timeout is wrong; force races with fake timers or interleaving.

units.text: Done when every hypothesis has one verdict and every confirmed one has its commit.

rules.rule: Verdict step is done when every hypothesis has one verdict and every confirmed one has its commit.

units.text: **Leave the branch for the captain.**

rules.rule: Leave the proof branch for the captain: the captain pushes it; the inquisitor leaves it committed and clean.

units.text: The captain pushes it; you leave it committed and clean.
Done when `git status` is clean and `git log` on the branch shows only your proof commits.
**Write the area's entries** in the return shape.

rules.rule: Write the area entries in the return shape.

units.text: A confirmed finding's `where` is the defect's `file:line`, not the test's; its proof is `red test <SHA> <test path>::<test name>`.
A confirmed register entry is a sighting with that proof.

rules.rule: A confirmed register entry is a sighting with that proof.

units.text: Every not-reproduced and inconclusive hypothesis goes under `Not reproduced` with its observation, marked `inconclusive` where it is.

rules.rule: Every not-reproduced and inconclusive hypothesis goes under Not reproduced with its observation, marked inconclusive where it is.

units.text: Done when every hypothesis on the list appears exactly once in the return.

rules.rule: Entries are done when every hypothesis on the list appears exactly once in the return.

units.text: An inquisition crew agent reads its own context size after each work item, and hands the rest of its area back once it is past its limit.

rules.rule: An inquisition crew agent reads its own context size after each work item and hands the rest of its area back once past its limit.

units.text: The limit is 110k tokens unless the commission set another, and your brief states it.

rules.rule: The context limit is 110k tokens unless the commission set another; the brief states it.

units.text: The rule is for inquisition crew only: you run long and autonomous, and nothing compacts your context for you.

rules.rule: The context-size rule is for inquisition crew only.

units.text: The threshold is a tunable for today's models, not a law.
The check reads the transcript of the session your environment names.
Inquisition crew run as their own sessions, dispatched through T3 `delegate_task` (DR 057), because they outlive the captain's turn.

rules.rule: Inquisition crew run as their own sessions, dispatched through T3 delegate_task (DR 057), because they outlive the captain's turn.

units.text: A native subagent carries its parent's session ID, so the script would read the parent's transcript.

notRule.note: native subagent shares parent session ID

units.text: Without T3, or wherever you are not your own session, the check is unavailable: write `unavailable` in the return's context field and keep to the rest of these rules.

rules.rule: Without T3, or wherever the agent is not its own session, the context check is unavailable: write unavailable in the return context field and keep to the other rules.

units.text: Save this script to a temporary file outside the repository, for example `<temp dir>/context-size.mjs`, so it never enters a commit:

rules.rule: Save the context-size script to a temporary file outside the repository, e.g. <temp dir>/context-size.mjs, so it never enters a commit.

units.text: Claude Code: the script reads the session transcript that `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` names under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and adds the last assistant entry's input, cache-creation and cache-read tokens.

notRule.note: how the script reads Claude Code transcripts

units.text: Codex: it reads the rollout log whose file name carries `CODEX_THREAD_ID` under `CODEX_HOME`, and prints the last `token_count` event's input tokens.

notRule.note: how the script reads Codex logs

units.text: Replace `<temp dir>` with the folder you saved the script in, and keep the quotes, since a Windows temp path can hold spaces:

rules.rule: Replace <temp dir> with the folder the script is saved in and keep the quotes, since a Windows temp path can hold spaces.

units.text:
```bash
node "<temp dir>/context-size.mjs"
```
The number is the model's input at its last call, so it trails your newest work by one call: read it after each work item, never once at the start.

rules.rule: Read the context size after each work item, never once at the start; the number is the input at the last call and trails newest work by one call.

units.text: Then:
**Under the limit:** start the next item.

rules.rule: Under the limit: start the next item.

units.text: **Over the limit:** stop.

rules.rule: Over the limit: stop.

units.text: The item you just documented is your last; return with every item not yet done listed as handed back.
The captain sends a fresh agent for the rest of the area.

rules.rule: The captain sends a fresh agent for the rest of the area.

units.text: **`unknown host`, or an error:** say so in the return's context field and keep working the area.

rules.rule: On unknown host or an error, say so in the return context field and keep working the area.

units.text: The third phase, wherever the landing changed behaviour a user can reach.
Drive takes the running app through the area's journeys and edge cases, the way a user would, so that it works as well as it reads.

rules.rule: Drive takes the running app through the area's journeys and edge cases the way a user would.

units.text: You change nothing in the repository; on a project with nothing to run, Drive does not apply and the area's map row says so.

rules.rule: Drive changes nothing in the repository.
On a project with nothing to run, Drive does not apply and the map row says so.

units.text: **Load the verification skill** your brief names.

rules.rule: Load the verification skill the brief names.

units.text: Read its launch and drive sections and the feature-map files that cover the area.
Done when you know how to launch the app at the audit SHA and how to drive each feature the area touches.
**List the journeys.**

rules.rule: List the journeys: every feature of the area a user can reach through the app or API, each with edge cases (empty, invalid, boundary, repeated, interrupted, concurrent where a user can cause it).

units.text: Every feature of the area a user can reach through the app or its API, each with its edge cases: empty, invalid, boundary, repeated, interrupted, concurrent where a user can cause it.
Add every register entry for the area tagged `drivable`.
Done when every feature of the area and every tagged entry has at least one journey on the list.
**Drive each journey** through the verification skill and the API endpoints, following the skill's launch model: health-check the instance before trusting it, and clean every drive's residue.

rules.rule: Drive each journey through the verification skill and the API endpoints, following the skill launch model: health-check the instance before trusting it and clean every drive's residue.

units.text: Capture what you observe: output, screenshot or snapshot, response body, exit code.
Done when each journey has an observed result.
**Judge each journey.**

rules.rule: Judge each journey: the observed result against the expected one from the intent, feature map and register entry.

units.text: The observed result against the expected one from the intent, the feature map and the register entry.
Done when each journey is `works`, a finding, a sighting, or `unreachable` with its concrete prerequisite.
**Name every verification gap.**

rules.rule: Name every verification gap: where a user can do something the verification skill cannot, it is a gap of severity should, owner maintain-verification-skill.

units.text: Where a user can do something the verification skill cannot, that is a verification gap: severity `should`, owner `maintain-verification-skill`.
Leave the verification skill as it is; the gap ticket fixes it.

rules.rule: Leave the verification skill as it is; the gap ticket fixes it.

units.text: Done when every journey you could not drive is a gap or `unreachable` with its prerequisite.
**Write the area's entries** in the return shape.

rules.rule: Write the area entries in the return shape.

units.text: A finding's proof is the rerunnable steps: launch, each action or request with its input, then the observed against the expected output.
A verification gap's `wrong` names the user action and the capability the skill lacks.
Each unreachable journey goes under `Unreachable` with its prerequisite and the route you tried.
Done when another agent could rerun every finding and sighting from the return alone.
The first phase on every area, and the only one on a prose area.
Read hunts what neither a test nor a drive would catch, and tags for the later phases what they can prove.
You change nothing.

rules.rule: Read changes nothing.

units.text: **Pin the area.**

rules.rule: Pin the area: in the brief's worktree at the audit SHA open every file in the area map row whole, not only diff hunks; git diff <landing base>..<audit SHA> -- <paths> shows what landed.

units.text: In the worktree your brief names, at the audit SHA, open every file in the area's map row, whole, not only the diff hunks; `git diff <landing base>..<audit SHA> -- <paths>` shows what landed.
Done when every path in the row is open at the audit SHA.
**Find the intent.**

rules.rule: Find the intent: read the ticket contracts, plan sections and Decision Records the brief names for the area, and any DR the area files cite.

units.text: Read the ticket contracts, plan sections and Decision Records the brief names for this area, and any Decision Record the area's files cite.
Done when you can say in one sentence what the area does and which intent governs it.
**Ask every question of every file**, relentlessly:

rules.rule: Ask every question of every file, relentlessly.

units.text: **Intent:** does it do what its ticket asked, all of it, and nothing it was not asked?

rules.rule: Question Intent: does it do what its ticket asked, all of it, and nothing it was not asked?

units.text: **Decisions:** does it contradict a Decision Record, the plan or a reference doc?

rules.rule: Question Decisions: does it contradict a Decision Record, the plan or a reference doc?

units.text: **Comments and docs:** is a comment, help text, message or doc wrong, stale or misleading?

rules.rule: Question Comments and docs: is a comment, help text, message or doc wrong, stale or misleading?

units.text: **Standards:** does it break `dydo/guides/coding-standards.md` or the code around it?

rules.rule: Question Standards: does it break dydo/guides/coding-standards.md or the code around it?

units.text: **Security:** boundary validation, injection, path traversal, secrets, authorization, unsafe deserialization.

rules.rule: Question Security: boundary validation, injection, path traversal, secrets, authorization, unsafe deserialization.

units.text: **Dead code:** an unused member, export or field, a path nothing reaches, a retirement left half-done.

rules.rule: Question Dead code: an unused member, export or field, a path nothing reaches, a retirement left half-done.

units.text: **Seams:** in a seam area, what each side assumes of the other, and whether both still hold.

rules.rule: Question Seams: in a seam area, what each side assumes of the other and whether both still hold.

units.text: In a prose area the questions are intent, decisions and contradiction: two passages, in the area or across it, that claim different things about one fact.

rules.rule: In a prose area the questions are intent, decisions and contradiction (two passages claiming different things about one fact).

units.text: Done when each question has been asked of each file.
**Prove what reading proves.**

rules.rule: Each finding made by reading carries its proof or is dropped as refuted.

units.text: Quote both passages at `file:line` for an intent, decision, standard, comment or prose finding.

rules.rule: Quote both passages at `file:line` for an intent, decision, standard, comment or prose finding.

units.text: For an unused member, run the reference search over the whole repository at the audit SHA and quote the command and its output.

rules.rule: For an unused member, run the reference search over the whole repository at the audit SHA and quote the command and its output.

units.text: Done when each such finding carries its proof or is dropped as refuted.
**Tag the rest.**

rules.rule: Tag the rest: a failure a test could decide is testable, one the running app could show is drivable, one can be both.

units.text: A failure a test could decide is `testable`; one the running app could show is `drivable`; one can be both.
Write the input, state and expected observation that would decide it.
Done when every unproved finding is tagged.
**Write the area's entries** in the return shape.

rules.rule: Write the area entries in the return shape.

units.text: A tagged finding carries the severity it would have if proved, and its proof field reads `tagged testable` or `tagged drivable` with the deciding input and observation.
A known bug in the area's register entries is a sighting.

rules.rule: A known bug in the area's register entries is a sighting.

units.text: Done when every finding of the area is a finding or a sighting line, or the area reports `none`.

Target: the code and tests one ticket delivered, judged against its contract and, when one governs, its pinned architecture plan and applicable feature-spec sections, on four axes judged alone, so a clean axis never masks a failed one.

rules.rule: The code review targets the code and tests one ticket delivered, judged against its contract and, when one governs, its pinned architecture plan and feature-spec sections, on four axes judged alone so a clean axis never masks a failed one.

units.text: **Pin the contract.**

rules.rule: Pin the contract.

units.text: The ticket description as of the brief's Linear `updatedAt`: outcome, scenarios, owned paths, base SHA, exact gates; governing standards, plan and applicable feature-spec sections at pinned commits.
Done when you can state what the change had to do without reading it.
**Read the hops.**

rules.rule: Read the hops: git log <base>..<candidate> lists the implement, fix and merge commits.

units.text: `git log <base>..<candidate>` lists the `implement`, `fix` and `merge` commits.
The implement hop is judged for doing what the contract says; a fix hop for closing the finding that sent it back and nothing else.
Done when you can say per hop what it changed and why.
**Read the diff, then the code it lands in.**

rules.rule: Read the diff (git diff <base>...<candidate>) then the code it lands in; read enough of each file to judge the whole.

units.text: `git diff <base>...<candidate>` gives the delta; read enough of each file to judge the whole.
Done when every hunk is accounted for.
**Work the four axes below, each entire**, every item verified against the source or a finding.

rules.rule: Work the four axes, each entire, every item verified against the source or a finding.

units.text: The candidate matches the pinned contract, the owned paths and the requested outcome

rules.rule: Contract axis: the candidate matches the pinned contract, the owned paths and the requested outcome.

units.text: Every scenario the contract calls for stands unweakened, and every scenario passes

rules.rule: Contract axis: every scenario the contract calls for stands unweakened and passes.

units.text: The `IMPLEMENTED` line the brief carries holds its red proof line: a Bug's reproduction failing with the fix reverted, a Feature's tests failing with the code stashed, an unused-member Bug's definition and reference search; rerun it only on a doubt you state

rules.rule: Contract axis: the IMPLEMENTED line holds its red proof line (Bug reproduction failing with fix reverted, Feature tests failing with code stashed, unused-member definition and reference search); rerun it only on a doubt you state.

units.text: Every behaviour, edge case and risk the contract names is claimed by a scenario or a test; a bug fix carries the test that reproduces the bug, an unused-member fix its definition and reference search instead

rules.rule: Contract axis: every behaviour, edge case and risk the contract names is claimed by a scenario or test; a bug fix carries the reproducing test, an unused-member fix its definition and reference search.

units.text: Nothing the implement hop had that the contract needed was dropped by a later hop

rules.rule: Contract axis: nothing the contract needed from the implement hop was dropped by a later hop.

units.text: Nothing beyond the contract: an unrelated improvement is scope creep and a finding

rules.rule: Contract axis: nothing beyond the contract; an unrelated improvement is scope creep and a finding.

units.text: Every deviation the implementation reported is justified or raised

rules.rule: Contract axis: every deviation the implementation reported is justified or raised.

units.text: `dydo/guides/coding-standards.md`, read from the repository root, and any stack-specific standard bind, the anti-slop mandate included, with the `codebase-design` lens on every seam the diff touches; a documented standard beats your taste, and a rule the tooling enforces is closed

rules.rule: Standards axis: dydo/guides/coding-standards.md (read from repo root) and any stack-specific standard bind, the anti-slop mandate included, with the codebase-design lens on every seam touched.
A documented standard beats taste and a tooling-enforced rule is closed.

units.text: The code the candidate touched is no worse than it was found, and smaller, simpler, standard or deeper wherever the change warranted it; an abstraction or optimisation ahead of a need is a finding

rules.rule: Standards axis: touched code is no worse than found, and smaller, simpler, standard or deeper where the change warranted; an abstraction or optimisation ahead of need is a finding.

units.text: Fowler's twelve smells (*Refactoring*, ch.

rules.rule: Standards axis: judge Fowler's twelve smells (Refactoring ch. 3): Mysterious Name, Duplicated Code, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Repeated Switches, Shotgun Surgery, Divergent Change, Speculative Generality, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest.

units.text: 3): Mysterious Name, Duplicated Code, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Repeated Switches, Shotgun Surgery, Divergent Change, Speculative Generality, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest.
Each is a question against the diff, the hunk quoted, a finding only with its concrete consequence named; every smell answered, not the first one found
Code that was already bad is a finding when this change builds on it

rules.rule: Standards axis: code that was already bad is a finding when this change builds on it.

units.text: Code that only tests call, or that is commented out, is dead.

rules.rule: Standards axis: code only tests call, or commented out, is dead.

units.text: The fix is to delete it with its tests, even when a gate asked for more tests or a refactor
Each test is a contract: one claim, named by case and expectation, at a seam a caller observes, that some breach turns red; a test with no such breach is a finding however green it runs

rules.rule: Standards axis: each test is a contract: one claim, named by case and expectation, at a seam a caller observes, that some breach turns red; a test with no such breach is a finding however green.

units.text: Shapes that pass by construction: an expected value recomputed the code's way; a mock inside the unit; a suite where no test was ever red; an assertion on a prompt file's wording; a metric moved with nothing claimed; an unbounded wait or a dependence on order

rules.rule: Standards axis: shapes that pass by construction are findings: expected value recomputed the code's way; a mock inside the unit; a suite where no test was ever red; an assertion on a prompt file's wording; a metric moved with nothing claimed; an unbounded wait or order dependence.

units.text: At a hop, the writer's affected-feature Light and applicable static run under the testing strategy, with every own/reached feature and parent-shared test accounted for; cheap checks and attributed failures carry exact-candidate evidence and owner disposition

rules.rule: Gates axis, at a hop: the writer's affected-feature Light and applicable static run under the testing strategy, with every own/reached feature and parent-shared test accounted for; cheap checks and attributed failures carry exact-candidate evidence and owner disposition.

units.text: At the declared coverage stage, read applicable coverage evidence for HCRAP on every method the change touched; one over the unchanged bar is a finding.

rules.rule: Gates axis, at the declared coverage stage: read applicable coverage evidence for HCRAP on every touched method; one over the unchanged bar is a finding.

units.text: This adds no per-hop coverage run; ordinary hop static checks remain required

rules.rule: Review adds no per-hop coverage run; ordinary hop static checks remain required.

units.text: The project's changed-code mutation gate, in its `--since <base>` form, run by you when the project has one; a surviving or uncovered mutant is a finding

rules.rule: Gates axis: run the project's changed-code mutation gate in its --since <base> form when the project has one; a surviving or uncovered mutant is a finding.

units.text: At a gate - the ticket's final gates, a merge, the landing - the whole set below on that exact candidate, read from its gate record or run by you:

rules.rule: At a gate (final gates, a merge, the landing) the whole gate set applies on that exact candidate, read from its gate record or run by the reviewer.

units.text: The ticket's final-stage commands: declared own-feature Heavy, measuring every Heavy-only source owed to it or failing; coverage producer/consumer at the scope Feature proof and gate placement in `dydo/guides/testing-strategy.md` sets for that gate (ticket-scoped at final gates and a Merge Sub-ticket, whole-stack at the landing and a default-branch sync, whole-stack per ticket where the facade records no feature selection), a changed line it misses failing; any mandatory integration/release suites; unresolved required failures remain failures, including inherited ones
Coverage, HCRAP and the one-level static policy in the project's testing guide
Mutation on the changed files, no survivor; one example value changed per scenario, none left green
`dydo check` when the change touches documentation or validation surfaces
Every boundary the diff touches validates what crosses it, and the vulnerabilities the standards' Security section names are asked against every such hunk; secrets stay out of source and logs

rules.rule: Security axis: every boundary the diff touches validates what crosses it, the vulnerabilities the standards' Security section names are asked against every such hunk, and secrets stay out of source and logs.

units.text: Logic holds at the edges (empty, null, first, last, off-by-one), no fallback masks an impossible state, and each error path is handled on purpose

rules.rule: Security axis: logic holds at the edges (empty, null, first, last, off-by-one), no fallback masks an impossible state, each error path is handled on purpose.

units.text: Ordering, concurrency and resource lifetime, where the diff introduces them

rules.rule: Security axis: ordering, concurrency and resource lifetime are checked where the diff introduces them.

units.text: Each finding, in a FAIL or a PASS tail, carries its severity and its axis in the `wrong:` slot, as `wrong: <axis>: <fact>`, the axis being `contract`, `standards`, `gates` or `security`.

rules.rule: Each finding, in a FAIL or PASS tail, carries severity and axis in the wrong: slot as "wrong: <axis>: <fact>", axis being contract, standards, gates or security.

units.text: Target: one documentation change delivered by a Linear ticket.

Two kinds arrive here: human-facing dydo documents under `dydo/`, judged against code for delivered behavior or governing intent for specs, and agent-facing documents (skills, their resources, entry points), judged as prompt files that must fire and route.

rules.rule: Two kinds of documentation change arrive: human-facing dydo documents judged against code (delivered behavior) or governing intent (specs), and agent-facing documents (skills, resources, entry points) judged as prompt files that must fire and route.

units.text: **Drift** is the failure both kinds share: a claim the tree no longer supports, or an environment restated in prose (directory layout, `--help`, config) where a pointer would not have gone stale.

rules.rule: Drift is a finding: a claim the tree no longer supports, or an environment restated in prose (directory layout, --help, config) where a pointer would not have gone stale.

units.text: Every item below is a finding when it holds, labelled with its severity.

rules.rule: Every item below is a finding when it holds, labelled with its severity.

units.text: **Resolve the contract.**

rules.rule: Resolve the contract: ticket description as of the brief's Linear updatedAt, and the governing plan and feature-spec sections at pinned commits.

units.text: The ticket description as of the brief's Linear `updatedAt`, and the governing plan and applicable feature-spec sections at pinned commits.
Done when audience, owned paths, acceptance criteria and gates are named; an unmet criterion or an edit outside the owned paths is a finding.
**Sort every changed file** into one of the two lists below, then work that list entire.

rules.rule: Sort every changed file into one of the two lists, then work that list entire.

units.text: **Verify from source.**

rules.rule: Verify from source: open the paths, run the commands, read the code; check the stage's exact-candidate gate evidence, `dydo check` among it.

units.text: Open the paths, run the commands, read the code; check this stage's exact-candidate gate evidence, `dydo check` among it, and rerun a gate only on a doubt you state.

rules.rule: Rerun a gate only on a doubt you state.

units.text: Drift lives in the sentence nobody rechecked.

notRule.note: drift lives in the unchecked sentence

units.text: Done when every claim the change makes has met its source.
Frontmatter, naming, or a link broken against `dydo/reference/writing-docs.md`, read from the repository root.

rules.rule: Human-docs finding: frontmatter, naming or a link broken against dydo/reference/writing-docs.md (read from repo root).

units.text: Written for a reader its folder does not name (`understand/` vs `guides/` vs `reference/`).

rules.rule: Human-docs finding: written for a reader its folder does not name (understand/ vs guides/ vs reference/).

units.text: A meaning another document already owns, written a second time here.

rules.rule: Human-docs finding: a meaning another document already owns, written a second time.

units.text: `dydo check` or a ticket gate left failing on the touched tree.

rules.rule: Human-docs finding: dydo check or a ticket gate left failing on the touched tree.

units.text: A reusable decision, invariant, pitfall or explanation left only in execution evidence instead of assimilated into dydo.

rules.rule: Human-docs finding: a reusable decision, invariant, pitfall or explanation left only in execution evidence instead of assimilated into dydo.

units.text: `writing-for-agents` governs this writing; the list below is that method turned into verdicts.

rules.rule: writing-for-agents governs agent-facing writing; the list below is that method turned into verdicts.

units.text: **Description that is not a trigger.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: a description that is not a trigger.

units.text: Model-invoked: leading word front-loaded, one trigger per branch, no identity the body already carries.
Explicit-only: one punchy human-facing line.
A crew role spawned by name may state its job, in trigger form.

rules.rule: A crew role spawned by name may state its job in trigger form.

units.text: **Anchor missing or doubled, or a tagline that changes nothing.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: anchor missing or doubled, or a tagline that changes nothing.

units.text: The no-op test grades against the model's default, and a failing line is deleted rather than softened.

rules.rule: The no-op test grades against the model's default, and a failing line is deleted rather than softened.

units.text: **Shape broken.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: shape broken.

units.text: Officers and crew: H1 → one-line job → Must-Reads → Boundary → Method with a completion criterion on every step → Return or Handoff.
A section order the user set for a role stands in place of Method; Must-Reads, Boundary, Return, and a completion criterion wherever steps exist still bind.

rules.rule: A section order the user set for a role stands in place of Method; Must-Reads, Boundary, Return and a completion criterion wherever steps exist still bind.

units.text: Methods keep their upstream shape.

rules.rule: Methods keep their upstream shape.

units.text: **Off the map.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: off the map.

units.text: Must-Reads that do not name what the sender hands over, a Return that does not name its receiver, or a sentence narrating what a neighbour does.
**A cross-reference missing or extra** against the exact set its brief binds.

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: a cross-reference missing or extra against the exact set its brief binds.

units.text: **Vocabulary off the dydo glossary**: a retired word anywhere, or a Linear noun away from a real handoff.

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: vocabulary off the dydo glossary: a retired word anywhere, or a Linear noun away from a real handoff.

units.text: **Steering by prohibition** where the positive target would carry it; a guardrail states both.

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: steering by prohibition where the positive target would carry it; a guardrail states both.

units.text: **Sprawl**: a document longer than its reader's path needs.

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: sprawl, a document longer than its reader's path needs.

units.text: Reference only some branches reach goes behind a pointer; a meaning stated twice is stated once.
**Upstream text altered without a binding reason.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: upstream text altered without a binding reason.

units.text: Linear, dydo and host bindings are the whole licence, and the attribution comment stays.
**A return shape its consumer cannot parse**: the review block, or a crew member's return to the Captain.

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: a return shape its consumer cannot parse (the review block, or a crew member's return to the Captain).

units.text: **Drift from the canonical source.**

rules.rule: Agent-docs finding: drift from the canonical source.

units.text: `skills/` is the single canonical tree, authored directly with no compile step; every host reads it through its own projection, never a generated copy.
Judge drift against that rule and the ticket's own contract.
Target: the tree as it exists after a merge.
Every merged ticket passed review alone; the seams between them passed nothing, and neither did the merge itself.
Read the integrated state at the scale of what landed: a two-file merge is minutes of mechanical checking, a whole feature is not.

rules.rule: Read the integrated state at the scale of what landed: a two-file merge is minutes of mechanical checking, a whole feature is not.

units.text: Scope is what this merge created or exposed.

rules.rule: Merge review scope is what this merge created or exposed.

units.text: Every operation has its own Merge Ticket: a lane into its parent, a ticket into the feature, or the landing.

rules.rule: Every merge operation (a lane into its parent, a ticket into the feature, the landing) has its own Merge Ticket.

units.text: Read that record's pinned source, target and combined gates.

rules.rule: Read the Merge Ticket record's pinned source, target and combined gates.

units.text: No review at another level substitutes for this one; final landing also proves Project acceptance.

rules.rule: No review at another level substitutes for the merge review.
A final landing also proves Project acceptance.

units.text: **Fix the unit.**

rules.rule: Fix the unit: name the merge commit, both parents and the tickets that landed in it.

units.text: Name the merge commit, both parents and the tickets that landed in it; diff the merged tree against the base the branch grew from, since each ticket's own review already covered its branch diff.
Done when every landed ticket is named.
**Sweep for merge artifacts.**

rules.rule: Sweep for merge artifacts: conflict markers, hunks that arrived twice, hunks that disappeared in resolution, a neighbour's change reverted by the resolution, build products or local files committed by accident.

units.text: Conflict markers, hunks that arrived twice, hunks that disappeared in resolution, a neighbour's change reverted by the resolution, build products or local files committed by accident.
Grep for the markers yourself; a clean build hides all of this.
Done when each has been searched for.
**Walk the seams.**

rules.rule: Walk the seams: every file, symbol and behaviour two merged tickets both touch (caller left on old contract, moved name, two implementations of one rule, broken assumption).

units.text: Every file, symbol and behaviour two merged tickets both touch: a caller left on the old contract, a name that moved under someone else, two implementations of one rule, an assumption one ticket holds and another broke.
These are the defects no ticket review could see, and why this pass exists.
Done when every shared file, symbol and behaviour is checked.
**Put the gates on the integrated state.**

rules.rule: Put the gates on the integrated state: each landed ticket's exact gate commands have run once on this exact merge commit; verify a gate record naming that commit, else run them in the merged tree.

units.text: Each landed ticket's exact gate commands have run once on this exact merge commit: where a gate record names that commit you verify it, and where none does you run them yourself in the merged tree.
A green from any other tree - an isolated worktree, either parent - proves nothing here.
Done when every gate has its command and result recorded.
**Prove acceptance** (final merge).

rules.rule: Prove acceptance at a final merge.

units.text: Run every feature file the landed tickets wrote, then read the governing plan and feature specs at pinned commits and prove each acceptance criterion against the merged tree, citing the scenario, command output or file:line that proves it.
A criterion you cannot prove is a finding.
Done when every criterion is proved or a finding.
The verdict goes on the Merge Ticket in the review block, naming the merge commit and every gate result.

rules.rule: The merge verdict goes on the Merge Ticket in the review block, naming the merge commit and every gate result.

units.text: Distinguish integration defects from defects in the source work so the Captain can route a fix here, or a revert and source rework; a later dependent merge requires a following fix ticket.

rules.rule: Distinguish integration defects from source-work defects so the Captain can route a fix here or a revert and source rework.
A later dependent merge requires a following fix ticket.

units.text: Target: one committed Project plan the map holder wrote for a cross-cutting architecture plan, proposed for human approval, or an amendment to it, judged in the shape below at the plan's candidate commit.

rules.rule: The project-plan review targets one committed Project plan the map holder wrote (architecture plan proposed for human approval, or an amendment), judged in the given shape at the plan's candidate commit.

units.text: PASS means the plan can reach human approval and open the first work; it certifies a starting route, not a complete one.

rules.rule: PASS means the plan can reach human approval and open the first work; it certifies a starting route, not a complete one.

units.text: **Check the shape.**

rules.rule: Check the shape of the plan.

units.text: Frontmatter carries `title`, `status`, `area`, `type` and `linear-project`; six numbered sections stand in order: 1 Specification (intent, in scope, out of scope, acceptance criteria, questions and answers), 2 Prior art, 3 Design, 4 Implementation ticket map (First pickable tickets, Later bearings, Exact gates), 5 Ordering and isolation, 6 Watch-outs; any Not yet specified fog closes it; `dydo check` passes.
Done when every required element exists or is one finding.
**Verify the ground.**

rules.rule: Verify the ground: read every cited Decision, path, pattern and specification at the candidate commit.

units.text: Read every cited Decision, path, pattern and specification at the candidate commit.
Done when every material claim matches its source or is one finding.
**Test the destination.**

rules.rule: Test the destination: intent, scope, acceptance and governing design agree, and each acceptance criterion names the scenario, command, diff or artifact that proves it at the final merge.

units.text: Intent, scope, acceptance and governing design agree, and each acceptance criterion names the scenario, command, diff or artifact that proves it at the final merge.
Done when the user knows what approval fixes.
**Inspect the starting route.**

rules.rule: Inspect the starting route: each first ticket is self-contained and vertical, carries outcome, owned paths, blockers, gate and base branch, exactly one Type, one Mode and Todo; its gate is copy-pasteable.

units.text: Each first ticket is self-contained and vertical, carries outcome, owned paths, blockers, gate and base branch, exactly one Type, one Mode and `Todo`; its gate is copy-pasteable.
Check status and priority against `dydo/reference/linear-workspace-standard.md`, read from the repository root.
Owned paths isolate parallel work, hot paths are serial, and the first merge order is credible.
Done when every listed ticket is safe for a Ticket Captain to claim.
**Respect the horizon.**

rules.rule: Respect the horizon.

units.text: Later bearings orient without speculative precision, and every in-scope outcome, the durable knowledge and the integration the destination needs among them, is a first ticket, a later bearing, honest fog or a blocking Question Ticket.
Done when the map starts the journey without hiding or inventing what comes later.
**Wayfinding fog is not a gap.**

rules.rule: Wayfinding fog is not a gap.

units.text: A sharp blocker left after authoritative homework and needing human judgment is a `Question` ticket in `Todo`, created by the map holder, recording its homework and blocking every ticket that waits on it, with priority by that standard.

rules.rule: A sharp blocker left after authoritative homework and needing human judgment is a Question ticket in Todo, created by the map holder, recording its homework and blocking every ticket that waits on it, with priority per the Linear workspace standard.

units.text: The map holder owns the review loop and presents approval to the user; the second FAIL is his choice.

rules.rule: The map holder owns the review loop and presents approval to the user; the second FAIL is the map holder's choice.

units.text: Dimmer uncertainty stays in `## Not yet specified`.
A plan that pretends either is settled FAILs; honest placement passes.
Target: the contract text on the ticket as it stands before any code, invoked when the Ticket Captain has bought a spec review.

rules.rule: The spec review targets the contract text on the ticket before any code and is invoked when the Ticket Captain has bought a spec review.

units.text: Judge it against the parent's criteria, the settled working tree, the governing Decisions, pinned architecture-plan and feature-spec sections, and the `code-writer` skill.

rules.rule: Judge the spec against the parent's criteria, the settled working tree, the governing Decisions, pinned architecture-plan and feature-spec sections, and the code-writer skill.

units.text: This review buys down material route risk.
A scenario beyond its parent criterion, a concrete contract conflict, a false pattern, a hidden design choice, a consequential missing case, or a gate that cannot prove the outcome is a finding.

rules.rule: A scenario beyond its parent criterion, a concrete contract conflict, a false pattern, a hidden design choice, a consequential missing case, or a gate that cannot prove the outcome is a finding.

units.text: Wording, formatting preference, and an equally valid route are outside this rubric: do not turn them into findings or notes.

rules.rule: Wording, formatting preference and an equally valid route are outside the spec rubric: do not turn them into findings or notes.

units.text: **Pin the ground.**

rules.rule: Pin the ground.

units.text: Match the contract to the target ticket or direct lane Sub-ticket, its five contract fields, base SHA, branch, worktree, clean state and owned paths.
**Done:** it binds the exact tree and nothing outside its authority.
**Judge the scenarios.**

rules.rule: Judge the scenarios.

units.text: Where the contract calls for Gherkin, each scenario stands at the product's boundary, in glossary words, deterministic, refining one criterion its parent carries; every example column changes an outcome.
**Done:** the scenarios say what the ticket proves and nothing the parent did not ask for.
**Verify the ground it cites.**

rules.rule: Verify the ground the spec cites.

units.text: Read every cited Decision, specification, pattern, seam, file, and test at the base SHA.
**Done:** each citation holds, or its departure is justified.
**Hunt hidden decisions.**

rules.rule: Hunt hidden decisions.

units.text: Walk the contract as the delegated writer through behavior, files, seams, edge and failure handling, migration, compatibility, and proof.
**Done:** no material choice is silently delegated to production.
**Check the proof.**

rules.rule: Check the proof.

units.text: Acceptance lines, scenarios and gates are exact and sufficient for the ticket outcome.
Run those applicable before code; mark implementation gates `not run - pre-code` after verifying their commands and pass conditions.
**Done:** the eventual result can fail as well as pass.
**Check the fog.**

rules.rule: Check the fog.

units.text: A missing answer is either found in the searched ground or returned through the Captain as a prepared Question packet naming its waiters.
**Done:** no assumption bridges an unknown route.
**Return the review block.**

rules.rule: Return the review block: PASS only when a writer can build the spec without being misled.

units.text: PASS only when a writer can build it without being misled.
**Done:** every finding states one material correction.
[ ] Exact Linear record, base SHA, branch, worktree, clean state and owned paths match

rules.rule: Checklist: exact Linear record, base SHA, branch, worktree, clean state and owned paths match.

units.text: [ ] Every scenario stands at the boundary, refines a parent criterion, and has no idle example column

rules.rule: Checklist: every scenario stands at the boundary, refines a parent criterion and has no idle example column.

units.text: [ ] Every cited Decision, pattern and path holds at the base SHA

rules.rule: Checklist: every cited Decision, pattern and path holds at the base SHA.

units.text: [ ] The acceptance lines account for every outcome without hidden design choices

rules.rule: Checklist: the acceptance lines account for every outcome without hidden design choices.

units.text: [ ] Edge cases, failures, migration, compatibility, and rollback are covered when consequential

rules.rule: Checklist: edge cases, failures, migration, compatibility and rollback are covered when consequential.

units.text: [ ] Scenarios and exact gates can prove the outcome; only stage-applicable gates were run

rules.rule: Checklist: scenarios and exact gates can prove the outcome; only stage-applicable gates were run.

units.text: [ ] Any unanswered question records homework and blocks the work through the Captain

rules.rule: Checklist: any unanswered question records homework and blocks the work through the Captain.
